$comment: Reviewed, accepted npm audit findings — machine-readable source of truth for scripts/check-audit.mjs. Keyed by (advisoryId, package), not by total count. Every entry here is a deliberate, documented deferral, not an oversight. See docs/DEPENDENCY_ADVISORIES.md for the human-readable rendering of this same data and the full reasoning, and docs/DECISIONS.md for the dated decision entries.

advisories.dependencyPath: next > node_modules/next/node_modules/postcss (bundled inside next's own package tree, not a top-level dependency of this project)
advisories.reachability: Production dependency chain (next is a direct production dependency of @missionthread/web), but the vulnerable code path itself (attacker-controlled sourceMappingURL parsing) is never exercised: this application never processes CSS from an untrusted or attacker-controlled source. postcss here is Next.js's own internal build-time CSS tooling.
advisories.fixNote: npm audit's only listed fix is next@9.3.3, a breaking major-version downgrade (fixAvailable.isSemVerMajor: true). Not applied.
advisories.reason: Unreachable in this application's actual usage; the only available fix is a breaking framework downgrade, a materially worse trade than the advisory itself.
